name: ADHD Cleaning Checklist
description: Cleaning broken into steps short enough to start, for anyone who stalls at the size of the job rather than the work itself.

items.text: Pick ONE room and close the door on the rest
Set a timer for 15 minutes
items.note: The timer is permission to stop, not a target to beat. Stopping when it goes off is the point.

items.text: Put on music or a podcast you already like
Carry in one bin bag, one laundry basket, one box for things that live elsewhere
Fill a glass of water and bring it with you
Ask someone to sit in the room or stay on a video call
items.note: Working alongside another person helps many people start. It does not matter what they are doing.

items.text: Walk the room and put only rubbish in the bag
Do not sort, do not decide, do not keep anything you are unsure about
Take the bag out when it is full or when you have gone round once
Collect every cup, plate and bottle onto one tray
Carry the tray to the kitchen
Put them in the dishwasher or leave them in the sink in water
items.note: Washing up is a separate job. Moving them out of the room is the win here.

items.text: Put every piece of dirty clothing in the basket
Put clean clothes in one pile on the bed, unfolded
Start a wash if the machine is empty

sections.title: Round four: things that live elsewhere

items.text: Put everything that belongs in another room into the box
Do not leave the room to deliver them yet
items.note: Leaving mid-task is where the session usually ends.

items.text: Deliver the box at the very end, in one trip
Pick the surface you see first when you walk in
Clear it completely
Wipe it
Put back only what belongs there
items.note: One clear surface changes how the whole room reads, which is why it beats cleaning three things halfway.

sections.title: If it is too much today

items.text: Do the five-minute version: rubbish and dishes only
Clear one square metre of floor and stop
Make the bed and count that as done
Set the timer for five minutes instead of fifteen
Leave the list where you can see it and come back tomorrow
items.note: A half-done room is not a failed attempt. It is a room with less in it than yesterday.

items.text: Keep a bin in every room
Put a laundry basket where clothes actually land
Keep cleaning supplies in the room that needs them, not in one cupboard
Use open baskets rather than lidded boxes
items.note: A lid is an extra step, and extra steps are where things get put down instead of away.

items.text: Pick one daily reset: clear the kitchen counter, or the floor, or the bed
Attach the reset to something you already do, like after dinner

faq.q: Why break cleaning into such small steps?
faq.a: Because the difficulty is usually in starting, not in the work. A step like "put rubbish in a bag" needs no decisions and can be finished in a few minutes, so it is easy to begin — and once you have begun, carrying on is far easier than starting was.

Having another person present while you work, in the room or on a video call. They do not help or supervise; they are simply there. Many people find a task far easier to begin and stay with when someone else is around, and it costs nothing to try.

faq.q: Why clean one room at a time?
faq.a: Carrying things to other rooms is the most common way a cleaning session ends — you leave, find something else, and do not come back. Keeping a box for out-of-room items and delivering them in one trip at the end avoids that.

faq.q: What if I only get halfway?
faq.a: Then the room is halfway better, which is the whole design of this list. Each round is ordered to stand on its own, so rubbish out and dishes gone is a real result even if nothing else happens that day.
